sentences.text: 1  2 M  ORDER 1]
They are heard and perused the case diary.
2] This order shall govern the disposal of all three applications, as all these applications have arisen out of Crime No.49/2024 registered at Police Station - Dawarkapuri District Indore.

3] All these applications are the first and second bail application filed by applicants, Rohit, Vishal and Deepak respectively under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 439 of Cr.P.C. as they are implicated in connection with Crime No.49/2024 registered at Police Station Dwarkapuri Ditrict Indore for offence punishable under Sections 365,376(D),323 and 506 of IPC/ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
The applicants are in custody since 12.2.2024, 25.1.2024 and 26.1.2024.

4] Allegations against the applicants are of gang rape of the prosecutrix, who according to the case of the prosecution, was abducted by the accused persons from 8.9.2023 to 15.9.2023 whereas the FIR has been lodged on 25.1.2024.

5] Counsel for the applicants has submitted that the dispute is going on between the husband of the prosecutrix and the applicants, which has led her to lodge false case against them and despite the fact that she had stated that co-accused had also threatened her on Instagram.

It is also submitted that no photographs, videos or instagram post have been seized during the course of the investigation, and the prosecutrix is also examined in the trial Court, and there are material omissions and contradictions in her statement.

6] Counsel for the applicants has also submitted that the prosecutrix NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20706 3 MCRC-26935-2025 had also made a similar allegation of rape against one Gattu @ Nitin, which was also compromised by the prosecutrix and is also admitted by her in the cross-examination.

It is further submitted that husband of the prosecutrix (PW-4) in his statement has also admitted that his wife had earlier lodged a report of rape against some other person and also that the matter has been compromised with the said accused and the husband of the prosecutrix has also stated that he and his wife had taken various loans from various persons.

It is further submitted that there is no tangible evidence available on record to connect the present applicants with the aforesaid offence and that the applicants have been in jail since 12.2.2024,
25.1.2024 and 26.1.2024 respectively, and the final conclusion of the trial will take a sufficient long time.
Thus, it is prayed that the bail applications be allowed.

7] Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer, and it is also submitted that against appliant Vishal Deepak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7201948/
2 there are three criminal antecedents, and against applicant Deepal there are seven criminal antecedents.

sentences.text: 8 ] Heard.

Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case diary and taking note of the fact that the FIR itself has been lodged after a period of around four months whereas no corroborating eveidence is available on record to prove the case of gang rape and the prosecutrix has already been examined who had earlier made similar allegation against some other persons with whom she compromised the matter and the fact that the applicants are lodged in jail since 12.2.2024, 25.1.2024 and 26.1.2024., this Court is inclined to allow both the applications.

9] Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, both NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20706 4 MCRC-26935-2025 the applications filed by the applicants are hereby allowed.

The applicants are directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with separate solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that they shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code,
1973.
9] Accordingly, both the applications are allowed and disposed of.
C.c. as per rules.
(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE das Deepak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7201948/
